sections.content: How many people are "health services and public health managers and directors"?

69,290 people

were counted on the census as "health services and public health managers and directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Managers and directors in this group co-ordinate the resources and activities of health care providers and purchasers at both district and unit levels.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "health services and public health managers and directors", 16.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "health services and public health managers and directors" was 16 to 19 years.

  • education managers
  • environmental health professionals
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "health services and public health managers and directors" there were more women than men (66.6% compared with 33.4%).

This means "health services and public health managers and directors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 33.4% and women made up 66.6% of "health services and public health managers and directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "health services and public health managers and directors" included:

  • teaching professionals (other)
  • legal associate professionals
  • tailors and dressmakers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "health services and public health managers and directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

The percentage of men and women who are "health services and public health managers and directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "health services and public health managers and directors", 9.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (83.6% compared with 16.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (91.9%) than self-employed (8.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
